name: @projexlight/hdk-video-editor
summary: Server-side video editing primitives for ProjexCloud: trim / clip / redact-faces / burn-in-subtitle on uploaded videos. Designed for the body-cam + Zoom-recording flow — caller submits a job, worker produces derived variants in sdk-media that sdk-evidence binds as variants of the source capture.

endpoints.description: Return the active editor's capability matrix (redact-faces / burn-subtitles / hw-accel-h264).

events.name: hdk-video-editor.job.completed.v1
events.description: Edit job finished; carries derived blob_id.

events.name: hdk-video-editor.job.failed.v1
events.description: Edit job failed; carries error class + retry-policy applied.

hooks.name: getCapabilities
hooks.description: Return capability matrix for the editor backend.

hooks.name: submitJob
hooks.description: Submit an edit job (trim / redact / burn-subtitle); returns job_id.

hooks.name: getJobStatus
hooks.description: Job state + percent complete + derived blob_id when done.

hooks.name: startWorker
hooks.description: Background worker — pulls queued jobs + runs ffmpeg pipeline.

scenarios.title: Trim 4h body-cam down to the 30s of interest
scenarios.when_to_use: Adjuster needs the moment-of-impact clip; trim job extracts + uploads as a new blob to sdk-media.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Job queued; worker produces the clip. Emits .completed.v1 with derived blob_id. sdk-evidence registers as a variant of the source capture.

scenarios.title: Redact bystander faces before sharing with customer
scenarios.when_to_use: Body-cam captured passers-by; PII-redact bystanders before the customer-facing release.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Worker runs face-detection + blur; keeps the customer's face. Emits .completed.v1. Variant ready for release.

scenarios.title: Burn captions into a Zoom recording for accessibility
scenarios.when_to_use: Customer asks for captions baked in (vs. external SRT); burn-subtitles job uses ai-gateway-generated transcript.
scenarios.expected_outcome: New variant with hard-coded captions written to sdk-media. Accessible to any video player without SRT support.

scenarios.title: Use GPU acceleration when the host has it
scenarios.when_to_use: Capability negotiation chooses NVENC H.264 when available; falls back to libx264 CPU encode otherwise.
scenarios.example_code:
const caps = await getCapabilities();
if (caps.hw_accel_h264) // worker uses -c:v h264_nvenc automatically.
scenarios.expected_outcome: GPU-accelerated runs 5-10x faster. Capability detection prevents crashes on hosts without GPU.

scenarios.title: Retry with software encode on hardware codec failure
scenarios.when_to_use: NVENC reports OOM mid-encode; the worker retries the job with libx264 automatically.
scenarios.example_code:
// inside the worker; failure caught + retried with op-rewritten params.
// caller sees the retry in getJobStatus as { attempts: 2, current_codec: 'libx264' }.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Job eventually completes; .completed.v1 carries the final codec. No caller intervention required.

compliance_posture.notes: Face-redaction is the GDPR + HIPAA bystander-protection lever for body-cam + meeting recording releases. Burn-in captions are the ADA-accessibility implementation. Source blob is preserved; variants are additive — original chain-of-custody never overwritten.

pricing_skus.unit_description: per minute of GPU encode (lower rate)
